full_judgment: 8. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned counsel for the petitioners the teamed Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties opposing the Rule controverted the submissions advanced from the side of the pre-emptor-petitioners and submits that it is the concurrent findings of both the courts below that the pre-emptor-petitioners are seized to be the co-sharers of the case land which was transferred in favour of the pre-emptee-opposite parties. The case kabla was registered on 28.12.1999 under section 60 of the Registration Act and the case holding was separated on 21.09.1991 at the instance of the father of the pre-emptors namely Narayon Chandra Banik. The vendor of the case land separated the juma in his name on 03.08.1999 and thereafter executed the case kabla in favour of the vendee. Admittedly; the original S.A. khatian is 20 and the mutation khatian is 554. This mutation khatian no 554 stands recorded in the name of the pre-emptor-petitioner's father vide exhibit-kha. Within the content of the case kabla (exhibit-ka) there is a recital that the father of the pre-emptors and the vendor of the ease kabla opened separate khatians. The learned Advocate further submits that the appellate court not considered the subsequent cancellation of the mutation case as alleged from the side of the learned Advocate for the petitioners is not correct. The correct proposition is such that both the courts below considering the facts and circumstances of the case held that the act of cancellation is mulafide which is 'after thought' for the very purpose of the pre-emption miscellaneous case. The learned Advocate also submits that the exhibited documents especially; exhibit-`ka' goes to show that after the death of the pre-emptor's father in imitation case No. 432(1K.T.)/1995-96 the petitioners has opened separate khatian pursuant to previous mutation case No. 554. Thereafter, at the instance of one Meghnath Paul an application under section 150 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 was filed on 29.03.2000 for amalgamation of the holding after cancellation of all previous mutation on the ground that no notice was served upon the co-sharers. It further appears that on the same date i.e. on 29.03.2000 without serving notice the order of amalgamation was given by the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Barisal. The learned Advocate submits that under sections 116 and 117 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 service of notice is a pre-condition of the order of amalgamation of holding. But the fact remains that no notice was served upon the co-sharers of the land. In this context; the learned Advocate referred a decision of our Apex Court reported in 37 DLR(AD)212. The Advocate lastly submits that both the courts below in their observation and findings concurrently held that the order of amalgamation would not help the pre-emptor-petitioners as because the kabla deed against which the pre-emption miscellaneous ease was instituted is prior to the amalgamation of the holding and with a malice subsequently the order of amalgamation was obtained for the very purpose of the miscellaneous case for getting the land pre-empted. There is no such illegality or irregularity or misreading and non-reading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice by which the impugned judgment and order can be interfered with.
